findings.highlight: The continuous world that was never completed
findings.evidenceJa: 果てず、翻らず、成らぬまま、連綿と続けられた一つの世界
findings.governingReading: One world continued unbroken without ending, reversal, or fulfillment
findings.explanation: Two of the three defining failures and the long unbroken succession disappear.

findings.highlight: it is still conscious
findings.evidenceJa: ソレにはまだ意思があった
findings.governingReading: It still possessed will or intent
findings.explanation: The English changes volition into mere consciousness.

findings.highlight: The swarm of worms fills the cavern.
findings.evidenceJa: この地下に棲み付いていた蟲の群
findings.governingReading: The swarm of worms that had made its home underground
findings.explanation: The worms’ established habitation becomes a present claim that they fill the cavern.

findings.highlight: even when using all of the worms
findings.evidenceJa: その全てを集め、一つの肉にしたところで
findings.governingReading: Even after gathering every worm into a single mass of flesh
findings.explanation: The improvised body’s construction is omitted.

findings.highlight: his soul’s vessel
findings.evidenceJa: 魂をこの世に留める本体
findings.governingReading: The principal body that kept his soul anchored in this world
findings.explanation: The English generalizes Zouken’s true-body relation into a vessel.

findings.highlight: he can’t heal his wounds after being killed twice
findings.evidenceJa: 二度潰された傷は癒えるものではない
findings.governingReading: The damage from being crushed twice cannot heal
findings.explanation: The English changes repeated bodily destruction into two completed deaths.

findings.highlight: What he yearned for, what he was about to obtain.
findings.evidenceJa: 永遠の具現を仰ぎながら
findings.governingReading: Looking up at the manifestation of eternity he had long sought and nearly obtained
findings.explanation: The object before Zouken is reduced to an unspecified desire, removing manifested eternity and his upward gaze.

findings.highlight: unable to familiarize themselves with the rules of the foreign land
findings.evidenceJa: 異国の法則に溶け合えず
findings.governingReading: Unable to blend with the laws of the foreign land
findings.explanation: The English makes structural incompatibility sound like lack of familiarity.

findings.highlight: he may have accepted fate
findings.evidenceJa: 大人しく滅びを甘受していただろう
findings.governingReading: He might quietly have accepted extinction
findings.explanation: The English removes the bloodline’s extinction and the quiet surrender Zouken contrasts with the truth.

findings.highlight: It has been three hundred years since the start of their search.
findings.evidenceJa: マキリの祖たる探求者より三百年
findings.governingReading: Three hundred years since the seeker who founded Makiri
findings.explanation: The English replaces the ancestral person anchoring the lineage with an abstract search.

findings.highlight: Three hundred years was their limit.
findings.evidenceJa: その三百年が魔術師の家系として限界だった
findings.governingReading: Three hundred years was the lineage’s limit as a family of magi
findings.explanation: The English drops the exact hereditary-magecraft constraint.

findings.highlight: The family died out in Zouken’s generation.
findings.evidenceJa: 臓硯の代で既に衰退していた
findings.governingReading: The Makiri magi had already declined by Zouken’s generation
findings.explanation: Decline is escalated to extinction, contradicting the surviving line.

findings.highlight: Matou Zouken’s life was a frantic protest against the end of the Makiri bloodline.
findings.evidenceJa: マキリの血族は所詮そこ止まりと突きつけられそれを必死に覆そうと抗ったのが、間桐臓硯という男の人生だった
findings.governingReading: Zouken’s life was a desperate struggle to overturn the verdict that Makiri blood could go no farther
findings.explanation: The English removes the imposed ceiling he spends his life trying to overturn.

findings.highlight: I don’t want to die, I don’t want to die, I don’t want to die, I don’t want to die, I don’t want to die, I don’t want to die, I don’t want to die, I don’t want to die I don’t want to die I don’t want to die
findings.evidenceJa: 死にたくない、死にたくない…………！！！！
findings.governingReading: I do not want to die; I do not want to die
findings.explanation: The English mechanically multiplies the refrain far beyond the two source repetitions.

findings.highlight: The rotting crumbling body. It’s painful. Nothing but pain.
findings.evidenceJa: 崩れる体が恨めしい。苦しいのは苦しい。とにかく苦しい。
findings.governingReading: He resents the collapsing body; pain is pain—above all, it hurts
findings.explanation: The English breaks the first thought into orphaned words and removes resentment toward the body.

findings.highlight: Suffering without satisfaction. Can’t disappear without leaving anything behind.
findings.evidenceJa: 苦しいまま死ぬなど出来るものか
findings.governingReading: How could he die while still in pain?
findings.explanation: A clause central to the escalation of his death terror is absent.

findings.highlight: The Holy Grail is right there. Grant the wish.
findings.evidenceJa: 目の前には聖杯が開いている、ならば我が望みを聞くがいい、問われれば答えてやろう
findings.governingReading: The Grail lies open before him; let it hear his wish, and if asked he will answer
findings.explanation: The English turns an open Grail and imagined question-and-answer into a direct command to grant the wish.

findings.highlight: The wish will come true on top of the cliff.
findings.evidenceJa: あそこまで、あの崖を登れば願いが叶う
findings.governingReading: If he can reach there—climb that cliff—his wish will be granted
findings.explanation: The English states a location but removes his required ascent and arrival.

findings.highlight: leaving bits of itself behind
findings.evidenceJa: ビチャビチャと自身を撒き散らしながら
findings.governingReading: Splashing and scattering itself wetly as it crawls
findings.explanation: The English removes the wet, self-dispersing manner of the crawl.

findings.highlight: it moves forward with tenacity
findings.evidenceJa: ただ怨念のみで前に進んでいく
findings.governingReading: It advances through sheer rancorous fixation alone
findings.explanation: The English repeats neutral tenacity where the source turns obsession into malign resentment.

findings.highlight: Ignoring the impending collapse
findings.evidenceJa: 崩壊の音も耳に入らず
findings.governingReading: The sound of the collapse no longer reaches its awareness
findings.explanation: The English changes perceptual exclusion into a deliberate choice.

findings.highlight: it moves forward to the Holy Grail
findings.evidenceJa: 聖杯だけを視界に収めてソレは進む
findings.governingReading: It advances with nothing but the Grail in its field of vision
findings.explanation: The tunnel vision defining Zouken’s fixation disappears.

findings.highlight: the hideous monster
findings.evidenceJa: この世ならざる醜怪
findings.governingReading: An unearthly grotesquerie
findings.explanation: The English replaces an otherworldly appearance with a generic monster classification.

findings.highlight: It looks up at the girl in astonishment.
findings.evidenceJa: ソレは陶然と少女を見上げる
findings.governingReading: It gazes up at the girl in rapt enchantment
findings.explanation: The English changes entrancement into surprise.

findings.highlight: His partner
findings.evidenceJa: 天の杯であった我が同胞
findings.governingReading: My comrade who was the Heaven’s Cup
findings.explanation: The English keeps companionship but drops Justeaze’s ritual identity and Zouken’s possessive first-person recognition.

findings.highlight: the eyes he adores
findings.evidenceJa: 彼が焦がれていた頃と同じ瞳
findings.governingReading: The same eyes she had in the days when he yearned for her
findings.explanation: The English turns a temporal memory relation into present adoration.

findings.highlight: The pure question shields his mind from the pain.
findings.evidenceJa: 苦しい、という思考が止まる
findings.governingReading: The thought “it hurts” stops
findings.explanation: The English invents mental shielding and converts a stopped verbal thought into pain itself.

findings.highlight: The species called humanity has set limits. To go outside the spiral of the brain.
findings.evidenceJa: あらかじめ限界を定められ、脳髄という螺旋の中で回り続けるモノを、外へ
findings.governingReading: Take the human species—whose limits are fixed in advance and which turns endlessly within the spiral called the brain—outside
findings.explanation: The English makes humanity set the limits itself, drops endless rotation, and breaks the object relation.

findings.highlight: to change his human life
findings.evidenceJa: 自身を、人という命を新しいものに変える
findings.governingReading: To transform himself—to make the life called human into something new
findings.explanation: The English loses the paired transformation of self and human life.

findings.highlight: the unimaginable land
findings.evidenceJa: 何人も想像できない地平
findings.governingReading: A horizon no person can imagine
findings.explanation: The English changes an unattainable conceptual horizon into a land.

findings.highlight: He can’t disappear until he makes it reality.
findings.evidenceJa: 至るまで消える訳にはいかなかった
findings.governingReading: He could not disappear before reaching it
findings.explanation: The English changes reaching the ideal into making it real.

findings.highlight: even after his enemies died
findings.evidenceJa: あらゆる仇敵たちが去った後も
findings.governingReading: Even after all his foes had departed
findings.explanation: The English asserts that every foe died where the source only says they left.

findings.highlight: He believed he had a reason to exist
findings.evidenceJa: そう在る事に意味があると信じ
findings.governingReading: He believed there was meaning in continuing to be that way
findings.explanation: The English turns fidelity to a mode of life into generic existential purpose.

findings.highlight: bring on a successor
findings.evidenceJa: 自身を継ぐ者を育む
findings.governingReading: Nurture those who would succeed him
findings.explanation: The English removes cultivation and narrows the possible successors to one.

findings.highlight: The Third Sorcery that was created by mistake, Angra Mainyu
findings.evidenceJa: 生み出された、間違いでしかない“第三魔法”
findings.governingReading: The produced “Third Magic” that is nothing but an error
findings.explanation: The English inserts Angra Mainyu as an explicit apposition and weakens “nothing but an error” into accidental creation.

findings.highlight: His journey is just starting.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼らの試み、その旅は始まったばかり
findings.governingReading: Their attempt—their journey—has only just begun
findings.explanation: The English reassigns the collective human project to Zouken alone and omits the attempt.

findings.highlight: The history to reach the distance starts its loop with an end of a dream.
findings.evidenceJa: 遥か彼方を目指す歴史が、ユメの終わりと共に回っていく
findings.governingReading: A long history aiming far beyond will begin turning with the end of the dream
findings.explanation: The English is malformed and obscures the forward historical motion.

findings.highlight: The voice is that of the old magus.
findings.evidenceJa: 諦める言葉は、やはり老魔術師そのものだ
findings.governingReading: Even his words of resignation are unmistakably the old magus himself
findings.explanation: The English removes the resignation that defines the final return of his familiar voice.

findings.highlight: Not hiding it until the very end
findings.evidenceJa: それを最期まで覆さず
findings.governingReading: He does not overturn that truth even at the end
findings.explanation: The English changes Zouken’s failure to repudiate his evil into merely not concealing it.

findings.highlight: the observer that also started everything
findings.evidenceJa: 生きながらえ当事者であり続けた傍観者
findings.governingReading: The observer who survived and remained a participant
findings.explanation: The English invents that Zouken started everything and removes his paradoxical participant-observer status.

findings.highlight: buried without trace by the crumbling rocks
findings.evidenceJa: 崩れ落ちた天蓋に呑み込まれた
findings.governingReading: Swallowed by the collapsing canopy
findings.explanation: The English changes the cavern’s falling overhead structure into generic rocks.

findings.highlight: as the embodiment of his desire is destroyed
findings.evidenceJa: 目指し続けた悲願の崩壊と共に
findings.governingReading: Together with the collapse of the cherished ambition he pursued without cease
findings.explanation: The English invents an embodiment and removes the lifetime act of pursuit.
